title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Findings and Demographics Predict Surgical Versus Nonoperative Management of Rotator Cuff Injuries: A Natural Language Processing Analysis.
abstract: To identify pathologic and demographic predictors of treatment selection and timing in patients with rotator cuff injuries using natural language processing of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports. Data were retrospectively reviewed in our institution's Information Commons database. Adult patients who underwent shoulder MRI within 30 days of rotator cuff injury diagnosis (1996-2023) were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes and categorized by treatment. A Generative Pre-Transformer-4 model analyzed MRI reports using a reference list of shoulder pathologies, with validation against a human reference for 50 reports. χ2 tests evaluated differences in shoulder pathology across treatment groups. Logistic regressions identified predictors of surgery-overall, as initial treatment, and after an initial trial of conservative management-while controlling for age, sex, insurance, race, and other imaging findings. A total of 3555 patients were identified, of whom 1139 underwent surgery. Natural language processing achieved 93.9% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity. Full-thickness supraspinatus tears predicted surgery overall (odds ratio [OR] 3.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.54-4.17, P < .001) and after an initial trial of conservative management (OR 3.14; 95% CI, 2.23-4.41, P < .001). Full-thickness subscapularis tears also predicted surgery overall (OR 1.74; 95% CI, 1.14-2.66, P = .011). Female sex decreased the odds of surgery (OR 0.76; 95% CI 0.64-0.90, P = .001). No differences in surgical likelihood were observed by race (P = .272-.986) or between Medicare and private insurance (P = .735). MRI findings and demographics were associated with treatment selection and timing for patients with rotator cuff injuries. Natural language processing analysis of MRI reports enabled the identification of pathologic treatment predictors. Level III, retrospective prognostic cohort study.

title: Editorial Commentary: Hip Microinstability: Stability Is the Goal, Plication Is a Tool.
abstract: Hip microinstability remains one of the most challenging conditions we encounter in hip preservation surgery. The difficulty is not performing a capsular plication but determining when instability is truly present and clinically relevant. In our experience, no single clinical, radiographic, or intraoperative finding should define the diagnosis. Rather, the entire clinical picture must be considered when evaluating the potentially unstable hip. Capsular plication represents an important component of this strategy but should not be considered in isolation. Careful diagnosis and thoughtful patient selection remain fundamental to successful treatment of hip microinstability.

title: Arthroscopic Lateral Tibial Plateau Translation Correlates With Pivot-Shift Severity in Anterior Cruciate Ligament-Deficient Knees.
abstract: To quantify arthroscopic lateral tibial plateau (LTP) translation in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-deficient knees using a standardized intraoperative protocol and to evaluate its association with pivot-shift grade and lateral tibial slope, including its ability to discriminate high-grade pivot-shift. Patients aged 18 to 45 years with an isolated ACL rupture confirmed by clinical examination, magnetic resonance imaging, and arthroscopy who met the predefined eligibility criteria and had arthroscopic video of adequate quality for measurement underwent standardized arthroscopic assessment of LTP translation. Arthroscopic LTP translation was quantified from standardized high-definition arthroscopic video recordings using a calibrated probe during valgus and internal rotation stress at 30° of knee flexion. Measurements were independently repeated by 2 observers. Associations with preoperative pivot-shift grade and lateral tibial slope were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Sixty patients (38 men, 22 women; mean age 29.8 ± 6.7 years) were included in the final analysis. Mean arthroscopic LTP translation was 4.6 ± 1.7 mm (range, 2-8 mm). Reproducibility was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient intra = 0.91; inter = 0.89). LTP translation strongly correlated with pivot-shift grade (r = 0.72, P < .001) and moderately with lateral tibial slope (r = 0.51, P = .003). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed an area under the curve of 0.85 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-0.93). A threshold of >5 mm yielded 82% sensitivity and 78% specificity for detecting high-grade pivot-shift. Arthroscopic quantification of LTP translation is a reproducible and clinically relevant method for objectively assessing rotational instability in ACL-deficient knees. Arthroscopic quantification of LTP translation showed excellent inter- and intraobserver reliability and was strongly associated with preoperative pivot-shift grade. A translation threshold greater than 5 mm showed good discriminative performance for identifying high-grade pivot-shift. Level III, retrospective comparative study.

title: Higher Preoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging Use in Asia-Pacific Compared With North America for Pediatric Tibial Eminence Fractures: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate differences in the incidence, diagnosis, and management of pediatric tibial eminence fractures between the Asia-Pacific region and North America. Methods A systematic review and subjective synthesis was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to May 1, 2025, using the keywords "tibial eminence" or "tibial spine" or "anterior cruciate ligament" and "fracture or avulsion." All original human surgical studies on pediatric tibial eminence fractures published in the Asia-Pacific region and North America were included, and data on the incidence, diagnosis, and treatment of pediatric tibial eminence fractures were collected. Results A total of 24 studies (9 from Asia-Pacific and 15 from North America) were selected with a total of 1973 patients. Subset analysis (of 6 Asia-Pacific and 3 North American studies) showed a trend toward higher rates of preoperative magnetic resonance imaging use among Asia-Pacific (96.3%-100%) compared with North American patients (36.2%-46.0%). There were also trends toward higher rates of arthroscopic reduction (compared with open reduction) and suture-based fixation (compared with screw fixation and other modalities) observed in Asia-Pacific patients compared with North American patients. Conclusions Asia-Pacific surgeons reported substantially higher preoperative magnetic resonance imaging use compared with North American surgeons, alongside potential trends toward greater use of arthroscopic reduction and suture-based fixation. Level of evidence Level IV, systematic review of Level III and IV studies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Predicts Failure of Nonoperative Treatment in Degenerative Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears.
abstract: Purpose To develop an artificial intelligence-based algorithm to predict success of nonoperative treatment in degenerative posterosuperior tears and to identify the most influential features. Methods Patients with degenerative rotator cuff tears initially treated nonoperatively were enrolled prospectively from January 2022 to November 2024. Exclusion criteria included age >75 years; <24 months of follow-up; massive, traumatic, and partial tears; arthritic changes (Hamada >2); and severe fatty degeneration (Goutallier >2). All patients followed a standardized physiotherapy protocol and could choose surgery if symptoms persisted; failure was defined as opting for surgery. Collected variables included demographics, comorbidities (diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and smoking), magnetic resonance imaging tear characteristics (size; International Society of Arthroscopy, Knee Surgery, and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine classification; associated cuff involvement; and biceps pathology), corticosteroid injection history, and functional scores (American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Subjective Shoulder Value, and the visual analog scale). First, a standard statistical analysis between groups was performed. Later, the dataset was split into a train (80%) and test (20%), and a random forest algorithm model was developed. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations values were computed to assess feature importance. Results Of the 412 patients enrolled, 347 patients met the inclusion criteria. After 24 months, 66 (19%) patients opted for surgery. Mean follow-up was 30.4 months (range, 24-32). Compared with the successful nonoperative treatment group, patients who failed treatment were younger (58.5 vs 64.6 years, P = .001) and had higher body mass index (28.8 vs 27.2, P = .016), greater subscapularis involvement (13.5% vs 3%, P = .042), higher visual analog scale scores (7.7 vs 7.2, P = .018), lower Subjective Shoulder Value (30.9 vs 38.9, P = .003), and lower American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores (40.6 vs 47.1, P = .001). The model achieved an area under the curve of 84%, predicting success rate of the nonoperative treatment with 94% sensitivity, 62% specificity, 89% positive predictive value, and 77% negative predictive value. The most influential variables for the model were age, tear size, and pretreatment functional scores. Conclusions The artificial intelligence-based algorithm accurately predicted nonoperative treatment outcomes in degenerative posterosuperior rotator cuff tears (area under the curve 0.84, sensitivity 94%). Age, tear size, and function were the main predictors. Level of evidence Level IV, prognostic retrospective case series.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Does Not Accurately Estimate the Size of Glenoid Labrum Tears in Patients With Shoulder Instability.
abstract: Purpose To compare magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based measurements of glenoid labral tears with intraoperative measurements. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients that underwent shoulder capsulorrhaphy between 2019 and 2024 at a single academic medical center. All patients with a single labrum tear, an MRI within 6 months of surgery, and historical tear measurements or measurable intraoperative photographs were included in the study. Glenoid labrum tear size was noted using the clockface convention described in "hours." When clockface measurements were not reported on MRI reads, measurements were made by a radiologist. When clockface measurements were not reported in operative notes, measurements were made by an orthopaedic surgeon using intraoperative photographs. A paired t test was used to evaluate any difference between the MRI and intraoperative measurements. Results Two hundred sixteen glenoid labral tears from 211 patients met inclusion criteria. Average age was 27.2 ± 11.8 years, 68.5% of patients were men, and 56.9% of glenoid labrum tears were right-sided. On average, MRI measurements exceeded intraoperative measurements (4.15 ± 2.90 hours vs 2.80 ± 1.59 hours) with an average difference of 1.36 ± 3.09 hours (95% confidence interval = 0.94-1.77, P < .001) and a correlation of 0.154 ( P = .023). A greater difference in measurement was observed among men compared with women (1.64 vs 0.74 hours, P = .044). Conclusions MRI overestimated glenoid labrum tear size compared with intraoperative measurements and differed substantially between the 2 modalities on a case-by-case basis, with men displaying a larger discrepancy in measurement difference than women. These findings indicate that MRI may be more appropriately used as a categorical tool for confirming the presence of glenoid labral tears, rather than as a precise measure of tear size. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective diagnostic case series.

title: Endoscopic Plantar Partial Sesamoidectomy for the Management of Metatarsalgia of the First Metatarsal Head After Arthrodesis of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint.
abstract: First metatarsophalangeal arthrodesis has been used to treat various pathologies of the great toe with good clinical outcome. First metatarsal head metatarsalgia can occur after first metatarsophalangeal arthrodesis. Surgery is indicated if conservative measures cannot alleviate the symptoms. If there is isolated excessive plantar pressure of the first metatarsophalangeal joint without significant sagittal deformity of the first metatarsophalangeal joint, plantar partial ostectomy of the sesamoid bone(s) is indicated. The purpose of this technical note is to describe the technical details of endoscopic plantar partial sesamoidectomy for the management of metatarsalgia of the first metatarsal head after arthrodesis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. This all-endoscopy approach allows partial ostectomy of the sesamoid bone from its plantar side dorsally and is a more direct approach than arthroscopic sesamoidectomy to eliminate the plantar pressure point. The extent of partial ostectomy can be titrated according to the intraoperative assessment of plantar pressure distribution across the metatarsal heads. The aim is to eliminate the pressure point underneath the first metatarsal head without excessive bone removal and create excessive pressure underneath the second metatarsal head.

title: Computer-Assisted Hip Arthroscopy for Portal Establishment and Suture Anchor Placement.
abstract: Hip arthroscopy is the gold standard for treating femoroacetabular impingement syndrome and acetabular labral tears. Portal establishment and suture anchor placement are crucial steps for ensuring the success of the surgery. However, because of the complex anatomy, deep location, and narrow joint space of the hip joint, the learning curve for establishing the hip arthroscopy approach and placing suture anchors for labral repair is arduous, with a high risk of iatrogenic cartilage and labral damage. This article describes a solution that applies computer-assisted navigation to these 2 key steps. Based on the patient's preoperative computed tomography data, this technique enables the reconstruction of an individualized 3-dimensional skeletal model, on which the clockface target of the anterolateral portal at the acetabular rim and the placement sites of suture anchors for labral repair are precisely planned. Intraoperatively, high-precision spatial registration between the preoperative virtual plan and the patient's actual anatomical structure is achieved via 2-dimensional to 3-dimensional image registration. With the assistance of the navigation system, the surgeon can accurately establish the arthroscopic portal in a single attempt without fluoroscopy and safely perform acetabular suture anchor placement for subsequent labral suture.

title: Prostate MRI vascular markers and erectile function after nerve-sparing prostatectomy.
abstract: Objectives To determine whether preoperative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI)-derived vascular markers are associated with baseline and postoperative erectile function (EF) and change in EF in men undergoing bilateral nerve-sparing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Patients and methods A secondary retrospective imaging analysis was undertaken using prospectively collected cohort data. Men undergoing bilateral nerve-sparing RARP with a preoperative International Index of Erectile Function-erectile function domain score (IIEF-6) and preoperative mpMRI incorporating dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences were included. MRI-detected accessory pudendal artery (APA), prostate enhancement ratio (PER) and corporal enhancement ratio (CER) were assessed by two expert uro-radiologists. Associations with EF outcomes were examined using correlation analyses and univariable and multivariable linear regression. Results Seventy-one patients (mean age 60 years) met inclusion criteria; APA was identified in 31 (43.6%). APA presence was associated with higher baseline IIEF-6 scores (mean 24.1 vs. 20.0, p = 0.043). Baseline IIEF-6 demonstrated moderate negative correlation with PER ( ρ = -0.30, p = 0.014) and moderate positive correlation with CER ( ρ = 0.30, p = 0.018). On multivariable analysis, APA presence ( β = 5.20, p = 0.019), PER ( β = -0.049, p = 0.017) and CER ( β = 0.040, p = 0.049) independently predicted baseline EF. Increasing age independently predicted lower baseline IIEF-6 ( β = -0.34, p = 0.017), while higher body mass index correlated with poorer 24-month IIEF-6 scores ( ρ = -0.27, p = 0.046). Bilateral intrafascial/intra-interfascial nerve-sparing techniques were associated with superior 24-month EF outcomes (mean 16.8 vs. 10.5, p = 0.028). No MRI-derived marker predicted 24-month EF or EF change. Conclusion Preoperative mpMRI-derived vascular markers, particularly APA identification, independently correlate with baseline EF in men undergoing BNS RARP, supporting a contributory vascular component in post-prostatectomy ED. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether intraoperative vascular preservation strategies, guided by preoperative MRI vascular mapping, influence functional recovery and can be integrated into surgical planning pathways.

title: Effects of Vitamin B12, Folic Acid, and L-Carnitine on Congenital Malformations Induced by Vitamin A Hypervitaminosis.
abstract: Background Excessive intake of exogenous vitamin A during pregnancy has been associated with congenital malformations. This experimental study aimed to evaluate whether vitamin B12, folic acid, and L-carnitine exert a protective or contributory effect on malformations induced by hypervitaminosis A. Methods Thirty-five healthy adult female Wistar albino rats and seven male rats were used. Pregnant rats received vitamin A alone or in combination with vitamin B12, folic acid, or L-carnitine for 21 consecutive days (GD 0-21). At the end of gestation, neonates were evaluated for gross congenital malformations. Brain, liver, and eye tissues were excised and processed for histopathological and morphometric analyses. Results No gross external malformations were observed in any group; however, significant growth restriction and multi-organ histopathological alterations were detected in the offspring. Histological examination revealed interstitial edema in brain tissue and retinal detachment in the eye. Hepatic alterations included sinusoidal dilatation, hyperchromatic nuclei, necrotic cells, and cytoplasmic degenerative changes; these lesions remained mild. Somatic and organ morphometry showed that vitamin B12 supplementation partially alleviated retinoid-induced somatic growth retardation. Conclusion Although maternal hypervitaminosis A did not cause overt external malformations under the tested regimen, it induced multi-organ histopathological damage and severe fetal growth restriction. Adjuvant supplementation, particularly with vitamin B12, demonstrated modulatory effects against retinoid-induced developmental suppression.

title: Ameliorative Potential of Green and Red Cabbage Extracts Against Teratogenic and Hepatotoxic Effects of Dimenhydrinate in Chick Embryo.
abstract: Background Dimenhydrinate (DH) is the first generation medicine used as antiemetic. It is neurotoxic in rat and chick embryos. Both green cabbage (GCbg) and red cabbage (RCbg) have many health benefits and red cabbage is also full of anthocyanins and may minimize oxidative stress in chick embryo. Material and method The study was designed to check the teratogenic impacts of dimenhydrinate and curative abilities of green and red cabbage extracts against dimenhydrinate in chick embryo through morphometry, histopathology and micrometry. Fertilized eggs were divided into six groups (n = 50): (1) control (Cnt), injected with 0.02 mL distilled water (2) GCbg, injected with 0.02 mL green cabbage extract (3) RCbg, injected with 0.02 mL red cabbage extract (4) DH, injected with 0.02 mL dimenhydrinate (5) DH + GCbg, injected with 0.01 mL dimenhydrinate and 0.01 mL green cabbage extract (6) DH + RCbg, injected with 0.01 mL dimenhydrinate and 0.01 mL red cabbage extract. All groups were administered on the zero day of incubation, and recovery was made on the 14th day. Results The embryos of DH exposed group indicated significant decrease in embryonic body weight (7.71 ± 2.82 g) and liver weight (0.03 ± 0.02 g) as compared to control group (15.58 ± 0.75 g; 0.35 ± 0.01 g). The prominent morphometric malformations were amelia, phocomelia, microcephaly and microtia. The hepato-histopathologic signs include decreased hepatocytes, irregular hepatocyte cords and sinusoidal space and de-shaping central veins. Concusion This study indicated that dimenhydrinate is teratogenic in chick embryo and both cabbages have ability to decrease birth defects and red cabbage indicated more positive potential compared to green cabbage.

title: Disrupted Sensory-Motor Network Integrity in Excessive Online Gaming: Insight From Multimodal Morphometric Mapping.
abstract: Introduction Excessive online gaming (EOG) is a transitional stage between recreational gaming and internet gaming disorder (IGD), characterized by impaired self-control and escalating engagement. Early identification of neural and behavioral vulnerabilities is crucial for understanding IGD development. Methods Fifty-nine young adults (30 EOG, 29 controls) completed structural MRI and behavioral assessments, including the IGD Scale-Short Form (IGDS9-SF) and the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS). Source-based morphometry (SBM) identified independent gray matter networks, while behavioral profiling and receptor-level mapping examined functional and neurochemical associations. Results SBM revealed six gray matter components, with one network encompassing the right thalamus and precentral gyrus showing reduced loading in EOG, which negatively correlated with IGDS9-SF scores. Behavioral annotation linked this network to sensory integration, attention, and motor-executive control. Spatial overlap with serotonergic and dopaminergic receptor distributions indicated potential neurotransmitter involvement. Conclusion Early alterations in sensory-motor networks and associated neurotransmitter systems may contribute to impaired self-regulation and heightened reward sensitivity, providing a multimodal framework for understanding the progression from excessive gaming to IGD.

title: Independent Validation of the volBrain CognitiveTree Automated MRI Pipeline in Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis.
abstract: In Alzheimer's disease, significant structural changes are observed in various brain regions, particularly in the cerebral cortex. The aim of this study is to contribute to the diagnosis of the disease by conducting comparative analyses between Alzheimer's patients and a healthy control group. Magnetic resonance images from Alzheimer's disease and healthy control groups, comprising 100 individuals in each group, were retrospectively obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database. Image analysis was performed using the CognitiveTree module within the volBrain software. In this context, percentage values for the right, left, and total volumes of 231 distinct anatomical regions of the brain were analyzed using various statistical methods. In the classification analysis of Alzheimer's disease and healthy control groups, the highest accuracy rate of 90% was achieved using the Random Forest and Bagging Classifier models. The parameter with the greatest impact on the classification analysis was the total volume of the inferior lateral ventricle. In the machine learning analysis conducted using a 20% test set, the highest AUC value of 0.95 was obtained with the Random Forest algorithm. title: Nanoprobe-Enabled Precision Imaging and Panoramic Boundary Delineation in Retinoblastoma.
abstract: Retinoblastoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in children. Its prognosis depends critically on accurate delineation of the tumor and its margins, early detection of small lesions, and timely monitoring of therapeutic response. Traditional single-modality imaging techniques are inherently constrained by trade-offs among spatial resolution, molecular sensitivity, and dynamic imaging capability, making them insufficient for the demands of precision diagnosis and treatment. In recent years, nanomedicine-based imaging strategies have emerged as promising approaches to overcome these limitations. Through rational design of nanoprobes with tunable physicochemical properties, active targeting capabilities, and integrated multimodal signaling, researchers have achieved more comprehensive visualization and diagnostic evaluation of retinoblastoma lesions. In this review, we systematically summarize the major imaging modalities applied to retinoblastoma, including optical imaging, ultrasound (US), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and photoacoustic imaging (PAI). Subsequently, the corresponding imaging probes and targeting strategies were discussed, which were developed to enhance the imaging contrast and improve the spatiotemporal resolution of tumor visualization. Furthermore, we highlight the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the rational design of high-performance imaging nanoprobes and in multimodal image analysis, emphasizing its potential to enable quantitative tumor and boundary delineation. Finally, we outline the key challenges that must be addressed to advance the clinical translation of nanoprobes, including the identification of novel targeting strategies, AI-assisted image analysis, the development of models that more accurately recapitulate the human ocular microenvironment, and the application of new biocompatible materials. Overall, this review aims to provide comprehensive and insightful guidance for the development of next-generation nanoprobes for the precise visualization and boundary delineation of retinoblastoma.

title: Pragmatic Screening for Sarcopenia in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Development and Internal Validation of a Prospective Risk Model Integrating T12 CT Indices and Routine Clinical Variables.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia or low muscle mass is common in non-small cell lung cancer and predicts poorer outcomes, but its assessment typically relies on CT-based skeletal muscle index at the L3 vertebral level. Standard chest CTs often omit the L3 level, leaving many patients without a straightforward muscle mass measure, so sarcopenia frequently goes undetected. We therefore evaluated whether thoracic CT measurements could reliably substitute for L3 SMI and developed a simple, accurate clinical tool to identify patients at risk of CT-defined low muscle mass. Methods In retrospective (n = 192) and prospective (n = 177) cohorts of NSCLC patients, cross-sectional muscle area was quantified on CT at L3, T12, and T4. Deming regression and Bland-Altman analysis were used to assess correlations and agreement between T4- or T12-derived SMI and reference L3 SMI. Candidate clinical predictors were selected based on univariate associations and clinical plausibility, and machine-learning methods identified five routine variables, which were combined into the Lung Cancer Patients' Sarcopenia Risk Model (LSRM). Model performance was evaluated in terms of discrimination, calibration, and risk stratification and compared with established clinical indices like BMI and the advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI). Results T12-derived SMI showed a strong correlation and minimal bias versus L3, outperforming T4-derived SMI. A conversion equation was established to estimate L3 SMI from T12. The LSRM, incorporating age, body mass index, carcinoembryonic antigen, C-reactive protein, and lymphocyte count, demonstrated good discrimination, satisfactory calibration, and clear three-tier risk stratification. It outperformed BMI and ALI in identifying CT-defined low muscle mass. Conclusion T12 measurements on routine chest CT can replace L3 for muscle assessment. The LSRM provides a practical bedside tool for screening patients at risk of CT-defined low muscle mass in NSCLC without additional imaging, supporting earlier risk identification and integration into routine care.

title: Tooth autotransplantation combined with bone augmentation for reconstruction of the esthetic zone: A case report.
abstract: Background Reconstruction of cleft-associated defects in the anterior maxilla is complicated by deficient hard and soft tissues, scarring, and altered anatomy. This case report describes tooth autotransplantation with simultaneous autogenous bone augmentation for replacement of a congenitally absent maxillary lateral incisor. Methods A 20-year-old male with agenesis of tooth #10 and previous cleft lip repair presented after 4 years of removable prosthesis use. Examination revealed horizontal and vertical ridge deficiency and residual oronasal communication. After surgical closure of the communication, tooth #20 was autotransplanted to site #10 following extraoral apical resection. Thin autogenous cortical plates and particulate bone harvested from the maxillary tuberosity were used simultaneously to augment the facial defect. An implant was subsequently placed at the donor site. Root canal treatment, direct composite restoration, and subsequent connective-tissue augmentation completed the rehabilitation. Results At 12 months, the transplanted tooth remained functional and demonstrated grade I mobility, probing depths of 1.5-2.0 mm, and no bleeding on probing. No definite inflammatory or replacement root resorption was identified radiographically. The soft-tissue contour was improved, although partial remodeling of the augmented facial bone was evident. Conclusion Within the limitations of this case report, tooth autotransplantation with simultaneous autogenous bone augmentation allowed fixed tooth replacement and reconstruction of the deficient recipient site. This combined approach may represent a clinically relevant option in carefully selected patients when the available bone is insufficient for autotransplantation alone. Longer follow-up is required to assess its stability and long-term prognosis. Key points Digital planning and a printed donor-tooth replica facilitated donor selection and recipient-site preparation while limiting extraoral manipulation of the transplanted tooth. Simultaneous augmentation with thin autogenous cortical plates and particulate bone may support tooth autotransplantation when the available recipient-site bone is insufficient, although graft remodeling should be anticipated. Autotransplantation of a tooth with complete root formation requires careful surgical handling, appropriate endodontic management, and long-term monitoring for root resorption and ankylosis.

title: Trans-Patch Retrograde Re-Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re-Entry Strategies.
abstract: Failure of true-lumen re-entry after subintimal wire passage is a well-recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73-year-old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans-patch retrograde access and dedicated device-assisted re-entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12-month follow-up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6-month follow-up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re-entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.

title: Post-Dengue Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism: A Case Report.
abstract: Dengue fever is commonly associated with bleeding complications, particularly in patients with thrombocytopenia. However, thrombotic events, such as venous thromboembolism, are rare and under-recognized manifestations, particularly during the recovery phase, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report the case of a 25-year-old previously healthy male who presented with high-grade fever, myalgia, and headache and was diagnosed with dengue fever based on positive NS1 antigen testing. Dengue infection was confirmed by a positive NS1 antigen test performed on Day 3 of illness, consistent with early acute dengue infection. The diagnosis was further supported by the patient's clinical presentation, including high-grade fever, myalgia, and headache in the appropriate epidemiological context of a dengue-endemic region. During the recovery phase of the illness, he developed painful swelling of the right lower limb and progressive dyspnea. Investigations revealed markedly elevated D-dimer levels, right lower limb deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound, and bilateral pulmonary emboli with right ventricular strain on CT pulmonary angiography images. Although dengue-associated thrombosis has been reported in the setting of thrombocytopenia, as described by Ghatak et al., the present case demonstrates that thrombotic complications may also occur despite preserved platelet counts, highlighting the potential contribution of endothelial dysfunction and inflammatory activation. This case highlights the paradoxical coexistence of thrombosis and bleeding risk in dengue fever. To avoid potentially fatal thromboembolic complications in patients with dengue, early diagnosis, prompt anticoagulation, and a high index of suspicion are crucial.

title: Mesiodens: Clinical Variability, CBCT Evaluation, and Surgical Management, A Three-Case Series.
abstract: Mesiodens are the most common supernumerary teeth, typically located in the premaxillary region. They may remain asymptomatic or cause complications such as delayed eruption or displacement of permanent incisors. This case series describes three pediatric male patients with mesiodens. One with single and two cases with double mesiodens. Clinical and radiographic evaluations, including cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), were performed for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Findings included delayed eruption, midline diastema, and functional discomfort. All supernumerary teeth were surgically removed under local anesthesia. Follow-up showed favorable healing and normal eruption of permanent incisors. Early diagnosis and timely surgical intervention are essential to prevent complications and ensure normal dental development.

title: Spontaneous Bilateral Vesical Artery Pseudoaneurysms Presenting With Massive Recurrent Hematuria and Obstructive Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report.
abstract: Spontaneous development of vesical artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PA) as a cause of life-threatening hematuria is very rare. Most of the existing reports are due to trauma or other types of pelvic surgeries/urological procedures. Incomplete hemostasis in these patients can lead to subsequent complications such as clot retention, severe blood loss resulting in anemia and obstructive AKI. We report this extremely rare case of a 35 year old lady with bilateral VA-PA causing recurrent episodes of massive hematuria and obstructive AKI that was ultimately resolved by selective embolization. A 35-year-old female presented with a history of gross hematuria along with clot retention and severe anemia. She also had signs of obstructive AKI which required her to have temporary dialysis. Cystoscopy showed intravesical clot but no bleed site was identified on initial evaluation. On contrast-enhanced CT scan, there were pseudoaneurysms found from both sides coming off from left superior and right inferior branches of vesical artery. Following confirmation by selective pelvic angiogram, we did a superselective embolization using micro coils and PVOH particles to occlude both pseudoaneurysms. This resulted in immediate cessation of hematuria, normalization of renal functions and stabilization of Hb values. At last follow-up done in 6 weeks' time, all symptoms had resolved and there was complete thrombosis of both the lesions seen on imaging. Bilateral spontaneous vesical artery pseudoaneurysm is a condition that must be suspected in a patient presenting with recurrent episodes of severe hematuria despite having undergone seemingly successful endoscopic treatment. Immediate imaging of the vessels and selective angioembolization is the surest means of diagnosis and treatment, thus avoiding further complications.

title: Giant Cavernous Hemangioma in the Mesentery of the Descending Colon: A Case Report.
abstract: Gastrointestinal hemangiomas are rare, and those involving the mesentery are even more infrequent. The majority of cases reported in the literature had mesenteric cavernous hemangioma of the small intestine. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first documented case of a hemangioma originating from the mesentery of the descending colon. Preoperative diagnosis is exceedingly difficult, and various imaging modalities may be inconclusive. The patient was a 71-year-old Asian male presenting with recurrent dizziness and fatigue over several months. Physical examination revealed a mass that was palpable in the left mid-abdominal region. Laboratory examinations suggested gastrointestinal bleeding and anemia. Abdominal CT scans revealed a large mesenteric mass in the descending colon. The mass was surgically resected, and histopathological examination confirmed mesenteric cavernous hemangioma. The patient showed no signs of recurrence in 1 year of postoperative follow-up.

title: Odontogenic Keratocysts in the Anterior Midline Region: A Case Series and Literature Review.
abstract: This case series describes three midline odontogenic keratocysts (OKCs) and reviews the associated literature. All three patients were male; two lesions were maxillary. All lesions were surgically excised, with no recurrence. A search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified 33 reported cases of midline OKC, including this series. Of these, 64% (21/33) were male, and age ranged from 6 to 80 years (mean 39.8 ± 20.3). The mandible was affected in 67% (22/33). Excision was the predominant treatment (94%, 31/33), with adjunctive cauterization in 30% (10/33) and decompression in 15% (5/33). Among cases with available follow-up, one recurrence was reported. OKC should be considered in the differential diagnosis of midline jaw lesions, supported by combined clinical, radiographic, and histopathological assessment.

title: Retained Colorectal Foreign Body After Suspected Chemical Incapacitation: A Surgical and Forensic Challenge.
abstract: Retained rectal foreign bodies are an uncommon but clinically significant surgical emergency. We report the case of a 74-year-old male with multiple medical comorbidities who presented with progressive rectal pain and obstipation several days after an episode of suspected drug-facilitated assault. Plain radiography identified a large metallic aerosol can, and attempts to retrieve it under general anesthesia using surgical clamps and a magnetic probe failed. Intraoperative fluoroscopy demonstrated that the can had migrated proximal to the rectosigmoid junction into the left colon, precluding transanal extraction. The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy with longitudinal colotomy, permitting safe removal of the foreign body without evidence of perforation or visceral injury. This case illustrates the critical role of intraoperative fluoroscopy when digital examination fails, the indications for operative intervention in proximally migrated foreign bodies, and the importance of considering drug-facilitated assault as an etiology.

title: Systemic Diseases and the Eye: A Translational Perspective on Diabetes.
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a global chronic disease that affects the whole body and not just glucose metabolism. In diabetes, non-invasive ocular changes can help understand microvascular, neurodegenerative, and inflammatory processes. This analysis looks at the eye as a biomarker platform for diabetes-related disease, with retinal imaging informing systemic pathophysiology and the emergence of AI-assisted approaches. With improvements in optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography, it is possible to observe neurovascular changes that can occur before the clinical onset of diabetic retinopathy. Issues in the retina have also been connected to problems with the heart, brain, kidneys, and cognition. However, much of the evidence for problems involving the heart and cognition comes from studies on people without diabetes. Also, most of the available data are observational, rather than coming from controlled studies. As a result, retinal measurements should be considered candidate biomarkers rather than clinically validated predictors or surrogate endpoints for systemic outcomes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has reached a phase of clinical maturity such that it can be used in the automated screening of diabetic retinopathy. However, it remains investigational for systemic risk prediction, such as for chronic kidney disease, cardiovascular outcomes, and cognitive decline. Equally, the therapeutic implications of retinal neurodegeneration and other imaging biomarkers are under-validated for systemic decisions. Before retinal biomarkers can be used in precision diabetes care, we need more diabetes-specific prospective studies to establish standardized measurements, the clinical meaning of thresholds, incremental predictive value above and beyond established risk factors, reproducibility, cost-effectiveness, and evidence of improved outcomes.

title: Redefining leptomeningeal metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer: From terminal complication to molecularly managed disease.
abstract: Leptomeningeal disease (LMD) is one of the most devastating complications of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), historically associated with profound neurologic morbidity and poor survival. Advances in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-based diagnostics, improved molecular characterization, and the development of central nervous system (CNS)-penetrant targeted therapies have begun to reshape both disease assessment and treatment expectations, particularly in oncogene-driven NSCLC. Available data suggest that outcomes in LMD are highly heterogeneous and are influenced by molecular subtype, performance status, systemic disease control, and access to effective CNS-active therapies. In selected patients, especially those with epidermal growth factor receptor- or anaplastic lymphoma kinase-altered disease, contemporary targeted agents have demonstrated meaningful leptomeningeal and intracranial activity, supporting more durable and compartment-specific disease control. At the same time, diagnosis still relies on imperfect but complementary modalities, including magnetic resonance imaging and CSF cytology, whereas emerging liquid biopsy approaches may improve detection and longitudinal monitoring. Treatment failure is further shaped by the pharmacokinetic constraints of the leptomeningeal compartment, where limited drug penetration contributes to therapeutic resistance. This review highlights the evolving biology, diagnosis, prognostic determinants, and therapeutic landscape of NSCLC-associated LMD, while emphasizing persistent limitations in diagnostic standardization, response assessment, and clinical trial design. It also underscores the need for leptomeningeal-specific end points, longitudinal CSF-based biomarker integration, and more inclusive trial strategies to improve evidence generation and patient outcomes.

title: Generative artificial intelligence in medical oncology: A clinically focused narrative review of large language, vision-language, and agentic artificial intelligence systems.
abstract: Rapid advances in cancer genetics and genomics, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and therapeutics have substantially increased the complexity of clinical oncology. Integrating large and diverse data streams into timely, patient-specific decisions provides a compelling rationale for incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into cancer care. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) encompasses several classes of models capable of generating new content. This clinically focused review concentrates on GenAI applications based primarily on large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), as well as emerging agentic systems that use these models to perform coordinated, multistep tasks. LLMs demonstrate substantial medical knowledge, strong performance on oncology-related assessments, and emerging capabilities in clinical reasoning. Guideline- and retrieval-augmented systems can improve concordance with expert recommendations and interpretation of complex treatment algorithms. LLMs and VLMs have been applied to documentation, patient communication, information extraction and summarization, clinical decision support, and multimodal data synthesis. However, performance varies substantially across tasks and clinical domains, with important limitations including incomplete or outdated information, training-data bias, automation bias, and confabulation. Agentic AI represents an emerging extension of these technologies in which LLMs or VLMs are incorporated into systems capable of multistep planning, external information retrieval, specialized tool use, and iterative evaluation and refinement. Early oncology applications include evidence synthesis, multimodal clinical decision support, radiology, pathology, surgery, and individualized treatment planning. With rigorous validation, transparent implementation, continual updating, and appropriate expert oversight, GenAI may augment oncologists' judgment, improve patient understanding and experience, streamline cancer care delivery, and advance personalized oncology.

title: Non-small cell lung carcinoma and its mimics on cytology and small biopsy samples: a practical approach aligned with the WHO Reporting System.
abstract: Accurate classification of lung tumors in cytology specimens and small biopsies remains a diagnostic challenge because of limited cellularity, preanalytical variables, and significant morphologic overlap among entities. This review summarizes key cytomorphologic characteristics and practical immunocytochemical strategies, and common diagnostic pitfalls encountered in the evaluation of non-small cell lung carcinoma, small cell lung carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, secondary pulmonary neoplasms, and uncommon thoracic entities in endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and fine-needle aspiration samples. Particular emphasis is placed on the appropriate use of limited immunohistochemical panels to optimize tumor subtyping while preserving material for molecular testing. Diagnostic challenges such as crush artifact, necrosis, reactive mimics, overlapping morphologic patterns, and the risk of misclassification of rare tumors are addressed with practical guidance for differential diagnosis. By integrating morphologic assessment with ancillary testing, cytopathologists can achieve accurate tumor subtyping, distinguish mimics, and provide precise diagnoses that guide clinical management and selection of targeted therapies.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastric Cancer: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Predictive Developments, Evidence Maturity, and Translational Challenges.
abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden characterized by substantial heterogeneity in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has been increasingly investigated for the analysis of endoscopic images, radiological scans, whole-slide pathology images, molecular profiles, liquid-biopsy data, and multimodal clinical datasets. This structured review summarizes recent AI-based developments in GC diagnosis, staging, prognostic assessment, and treatment-response prediction, with particular emphasis on the translational maturity of the available evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant English-language publications from database inception through January 2026. Eligible studies were evaluated according to clinical task, data modality, model type, cohort size, study design, validation strategy, interpretability, clinical workflow readiness, and reported limitations. Recent findings Recent AI models have demonstrated promising performance in selected research settings, particularly in endoscopic image analysis, computational pathology, CT-based radiomics, and multimodal prognostic modeling. However, most studies remain retrospective, single-center, and internally validated. Calibration, robustness, prospective clinical utility, and generalizability across populations and institutions remain insufficiently assessed. Major barriers to translation include data heterogeneity, annotation variability, overfitting, data leakage, external validation failure, algorithmic bias, regulatory requirements, reimbursement, clinician-AI interaction, medicolegal responsibility, post-deployment monitoring, and model drift. Conclusion AI has considerable potential to support GC diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning, but most current models remain insufficiently validated for routine clinical use. Future progress will depend on transparent reporting, standardized validation, multicenter prospective trials, clinically meaningful endpoints, and the integration of explainable, trustworthy AI systems into routine clinical workflows.

Major barriers to translation include data heterogeneity, annotation variability, overfitting, data leakage, external validation failure, algorithmic bias, regulatory requirements, reimbursement, clinician-AI interaction, medicolegal responsibility, post-deployment monitoring, and model drift.

Conclusion

AI has considerable potential to support GC diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning, but most current models remain insufficiently validated for routine clinical use. Future progress will depend on transparent reporting, standardized validation, multicenter prospective trials, clinically meaningful endpoints, and the integration of explainable, trustworthy AI systems into routine clinical workflows.

title: Integrating Multimodal MRI Habitat and Transformer-Based Pathomics to Predict High-Risk Molecular Subtypes and Explore Biological Mechanisms in Adult Diffuse Gliomas.
abstract: Background This study aims to achieve accurate prediction of high-risk molecular subtypes of gliomas through a cross-scale Combined model, matching the model's classification metrics with patient risk stratification and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms. Methods This study retrospectively collected preoperative MRI, postoperative whole-slide pathological images, molecular markers, and clinical data from 456 adult diffuse glioma patients. We separately constructed an MRI habitat prediction model, a WSI Transformer-based deep learning pathomics (PDL) model, and a Combined model. A dynamic nomogram web page for predicting high-risk molecular subtypes was developed based on the Combined model. Patients were stratified into risk groups according to the output scores of the Combined model, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and the Log-rank test were employed to evaluate survival differences between the groups. Additionally, differential expression and GO/KEGG enrichment analyses were further performed in the test set with available RNA-seq data to explore transcriptional features and biological processes associated with model-based risk stratification. Results The Combined model demonstrated the highest AUC (Training set: 0.888, Test set: 0.836) compared to the Habitat model (Training set: 0.832, Test set: 0.798) and the PDL model (Training set: 0.852, Test set: 0.821). The high-risk and low-risk groups, stratified based on the cutoff value derived from the Combined model output scores, exhibited significant survival differences. Exploratory transcriptomic analysis showed that differentially expressed genes between the high- and low-risk groups were mainly enriched in biological processes and pathways related to the extracellular matrix and cell-matrix interactions. Conclusion The cross-scale Combined model not only enabled identification of high-risk molecular subtypes and risk stratification but also showed associations with biologically relevant transcriptional features.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease-Related Depression: From Visual Scoring to Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: Background Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is the key pathological basis of vascular depression. The precise identification of its neuroimaging markers is of core value for early diagnosis, elucidation of its pathological mechanism, and individualized treatment. Recent advances in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled automated, high-throughput characterization of CSVD-related brain lesions. However, the translation of these technical advances into clinical tools for depression-specific prediction and classification remains at an early stage. Results and conclusion This manuscript aims to summarize the application of traditional visual scoring systems in assessing the burden of CSVD and its association with depressive symptoms. Review the current status of imaging and AI research on CSVD-related depression. To provide a direction for the development of more precise and efficient imaging diagnostic tools for the future, and ultimately promote the practical application and utilization of precision medicine in the field of CSVD-related depression.

title: Radiomics-Assisted Preoperative Subtyping of Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas: A Retrospective Study Aligned With the WHO 2021 Classification.
abstract: Optimal surgical management of adult-type diffuse gliomas (ADGs) varies substantially by subtype, making accurate preoperative subtyping crucial for individualized surgical planning. This study aimed to develop a radiomics-based model for preoperative subtyping of ADG in accordance with the 2021 World Health Organization (WHO) Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors. A total of 382 patients with ADGs were enrolled and randomly assigned to a training set (n = 267) and an independent test set (n = 115). Tumor masks were automatically segmented and refined by experienced neurosurgeons. Radiomics features were extracted from MRI after standardized preprocessing and dimensionality reduction. Fourteen machine learning classifiers were evaluated, and the best-performing model was optimized and validated on the independent test set. Model performance was assessed using AUC, accuracy, recall, precision, F1 score, Kappa coefficient, and Matthews correlation coefficient. After LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression, 50 key features were retained. Random Forest showed the best preliminary performance and was selected for optimization. On the independent test set, the optimized model achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.9084, with favorable results across other metrics. Texture features contributed most strongly to prediction. This radiomics model enables robust preoperative ADG subtyping under the 2021 WHO classification and may support individualized surgical planning using routine MRI features. Owing to its retrospective single-center design, multicenter prospective external validation is required prior to widespread clinical application.

title: Site-Specific Associations Between CBCT-Derived Gray Value and Fractal Dimension and DEXA T-Scores in Postmenopausal Women: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a silent systemic skeletal disease characterized by microarchitectural deterioration and increased fracture risk; thus, early case-finding is essential. Although dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) is the reference standard for bone mineral density (BMD) assessment, limited accessibility and cost restrict its use for large-scale screening. Given that cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is routinely obtained in dental practice, image-derived parameters-gray value (GV) and fractal dimension (FD)-may provide insight into their association with systemic bone mineral density measured by DEXA in postmenopausal women, without additional radiation exposure. This cross-sectional study included 63 postmenopausal women aged 50-70 years undergoing dental CBCT (NewTom 3G; standardized acquisition). Six trabecular regions of interest (ROIs) were evaluated: mandibular retromolar, mandibular premolar, mandibular anterior (central), maxillary premolar, maxillary anterior (central), and maxillary tuberosity. GV values were extracted using OnDemand3D-Dental from standardized 25 × 25-pixel ROIs positioned to exclude cortical bone and dental structures. FD was calculated in ImageJ using a box-counting method following Gaussian blur subtraction, binarization, and skeletonization. Lumbar spine and hip BMD were measured by DEXA and categorized according to WHO criteria. Statistical analyses included t-tests/ANOVA, Pearson correlation (α = 0.05). Intra-observer reliability was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). DEXA classified 49.2% as normal, 34.9% as osteopenic, and 15.9% as osteoporotic. Lumbar assessment identified more non-normal cases than the hip evaluation. Reliability was good (ICC > 0.70). Although mean GV and FD did not differ significantly between groups, site-specific GV-FD correlations were observed. Notably, FD at the maxillary premolar correlated with lumbar T-scores in the non-normal group (p = 0.030). While GV and FD did not discriminate BMD categories overall, region-dependent associations between CBCT-derived parameters and systemic BMD were observed, suggesting potential clinical relevance in dental imaging. These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as diagnostic or screening indicators and require confirmation in larger studies.

title: Prevalence, Risk Indicators, and Patient-Reported Outcomes of Labial Gingival Recession Following Orthodontic Treatment: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Objectives To assess the prevalence, distribution, and risk indicators of gingival recession (GR) following orthodontic treatment (OT) in both private and hospital-based settings, and to evaluate its impact on patient satisfaction and willingness to seek corrective treatment. Materials and methods Clinical and radiographic records from baseline to follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. Additionally, participants completed a survey on satisfaction, perception of GR if present, and willingness to seek corrective treatment. Incident and persistent GR were analyzed separately. Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression with weakly informative priors was used to identify risk indicators for incident GR. Results A total of 103 patients (2030 teeth; mean age: 20.7 ± 9.7 years) were included. GR prevalence increased from 1.7% at baseline to 2.0% at appliance removal and continued to rise during the retention phase (3%-5%), with a site-specific distribution. Among 1996 teeth free of GR at baseline, 49 developed incident GR. A thin-scalloped gingival phenotype was the strongest risk indicator for incident GR (OR = 4.10; 95% CrI: 1.25-13.46). Most baseline GR persisted throughout follow-up. Satisfaction with OT remained high (mean score: 8.99 ± 1.04 on a 10-point scale) and was not significantly influenced by GR or treatment setting. Conclusions Gingival recession occurrence after orthodontic treatment is time- and site-dependent. A thin-scalloped gingival phenotype is the main risk indicator for incident GR, whereas pre-existing recession is highly persistent. Despite its occurrence, gingival recession had limited impact on patient satisfaction. Clinical relevance This study provides long-term, multicenter data on gingival recession following orthodontic treatment, and is the first to assess its impact on patient perception. The findings may help inform risk-based treatment planning and individualized patient counseling in orthodontic care.

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
abstract: Objectives To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. Methods This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. Results Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. Conclusions The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. Trial registration UMIN000053211.

In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified.

Conclusions

The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation.

title: Structural Reorganization of Hypothalamic Subfields in Postherpetic Neuralgia: Volumetric and Morphometric Covariance Network Analyses.
abstract: Background Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) is a chronic neuropathic pain condition associated with central nervous system reorganization, but hypothalamic alterations remain poorly understood. We investigated hypothalamic subfield volumes and morphometric covariance network organization in patients with PHN. Methods This prospective cross-sectional study included 42 patients with PHN and 41 healthy controls whose hypothalamic subfield volumes were obtained from T1-weighted MRI using automated FreeSurfer segmentation. Bilateral mean raw subfield volumes were compared between groups using analysis of covariance, adjusting for age, sex and estimated total intracranial volume, with false discovery rate correction for multiple comparisons. Morphometric covariance networks were constructed from age- and sex-residualized subfield volumes and graph-theoretical measures were compared using permutation testing. Results After adjustment for estimated total intracranial volume, age and sex, the tubular superior subfield was nominally larger in PHN (adjusted difference, 4.95 mm 3 ; 95% CI, 0.05-9.85; p = 0.048), but did not survive FDR correction. No other subfield or whole-hypothalamic volume differed significantly. PHN showed reduced local efficiency and clustering coefficient and increased characteristic path length, without a significant difference in global efficiency. No pain-side-dependent lateralization or significant associations between subfield volumes and pain measures or disease duration were observed. Conclusions PHN was associated with altered hypothalamic morphometric covariance organization, characterized by reduced local network segregation and increased characteristic path length, while regional volume differences were limited after intracranial volume correction. These findings suggest that PHN-related central reorganization may involve hypothalamic systems related to homeostatic regulation and stress adaptation. Significance statement This study demonstrates altered morphometric covariance organization of hypothalamic subfields in postherpetic neuralgia, despite limited evidence of regional volumetric differences after intracranial volume adjustment. These findings suggest that hypothalamic involvement in PHN may be better reflected by altered coordinated structural organization than by regional volume changes alone.

title: Pragmatic screening for autoimmune-associated epilepsy in drug-resistant epilepsy of unknown etiology in resource-limited settings: A hypothesis-generating study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the feasibility of investigating autoimmune etiology in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) of unknown origin in resource-limited settings and to develop a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating screening approach to guide autoantibody testing. Methods A prospective observational study including adults with DRE of unknown etiology was conducted at a tertiary epilepsy center in Brazil. All patients underwent standardized assessment including inflammatory and autoimmunity markers, brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis, and application of the APE2 and ACES scores. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings were analyzed in the context of published autoimmune-associated epilepsy (AAE) profiles to inform a pragmatic screening strategy. Results Twenty-six patients (46.2% female; median epilepsy duration: 18.5 years) were included. EEG findings were nonspecific. Six patients developed mesial temporal abnormalities on follow-up MRI. CSF protein elevation was observed in 37.5%, oligoclonal bands in 13.6%, and elevated IgG index in 18.2%. Antinuclear antibodies were detected in 26.9%. APE2 score ≥ 4 was present in 57.7%, while ACES score ≥ 2 occurred in 11.5%. Due to limited access to antibody testing, only one patient underwent CSF autoantibody analysis, confirming high-titer anti-GAD65. Based on integrated clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings, a pragmatic screening algorithm was proposed to prioritize candidates for autoantibody testing. Significance In resource-limited settings, systematic use of accessible clinical and laboratory markers may help identify patients with higher pre-test probability of AAE. A pragmatic screening approach may improve diagnostic efficiency and support individualized decision-making when comprehensive antibody testing is not readily available.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of cortical activity and remains central to the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of iEEG data increasingly challenge conventional visual interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have accelerated quantitative analyses in electrophysiology, supporting localization, outcome prediction, and therapeutic decision-making in epilepsy. This article reviews recent advances in the application of AI to iEEG in epilepsy and in particular stereo-EEG, although the concepts discussed are broadly relevant across iEEG modalities. Although many of these approaches have shown encouraging results, the current evidence remains largely preliminary, with most studies being retrospective, single-center investigations that lack independent external validation. AI-based integration of iEEG with multimodal magnetic resonance imaging shows promise for improving surgical planning in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Concurrently, early studies suggest that AI-driven iEEG analysis may enhance epileptogenic zone identification by detecting subtle electrophysiological signatures, network interactions, and temporal dynamics. These multimodal frameworks emphasize distributed epileptic networks rather than isolated focal abnormalities. AI is also reshaping how iEEG-guided stimulation is designed and interpreted. Data-driven approaches have the potential to optimize stimulation parameters, predict network responses, and clarify mechanisms underlying diagnostic and therapeutic stimulation, laying the groundwork for adaptive, patient-specific neuromodulation. Beyond short-term epilepsy monitoring, AI applications increasingly incorporate continuous sensing, longitudinal network modeling, and integration with implantable neurotechnology platforms. Although these developments require prospective multicenter studies with external validation before widespread clinical implementation, advances in multimodal data integration, interpretable modeling, and continuous sensing position AI-enhanced iEEG as an emerging platform for precision brain network medicine for epilepsy.

title: Limited sex-specific structural alterations across common epilepsies: A worldwide ENIGMA study.
abstract: Objective Epilepsy is characterized by widespread cortical and subcortical structural alterations beyond the epileptic zone. Importantly, the clinical manifestation of epilepsy, including seizure types, psychiatric comorbidities, and treatment responses, has been shown to differ between sexes. However, sex differences in structural alterations in epilepsy are seldomly reported in neuroimaging studies, partly due to limited sample sizes and single-center designs. We therefore tested whether epilepsy-related structural alterations differ between males and females, and whether the associations between structural measures and clinical characteristics vary by sex. Methods We analyzed clinician-assigned biological sex differences in common epilepsies and their related clinical variables using structural neuroimaging biomarkers in an international multicenter cohort of 1253 epilepsy patients and 1077 healthy controls. We studied cortical thickness and subcortical volume in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE). Results Both male and female patients with TLE showed widespread cortical and subcortical alterations in sex-stratified analyses, whereas GGE showed more extensive alterations in female patients and only subtle alterations in male patients. However, no significant sex-by-diagnosis interactions were identified in either the TLE (t = -2.153 to 1.705, all p FDR >.05) or GGE (t = -1.797 to 2.774, all p FDR >.05) cohort. Likewise, no significant interactions were found between sex and age at onset (t TLE = -1.835 to 1.092, t GGE = -2.394 to 1.392, all p FDR >.05) or disease duration (t TLE = -2.643 to 2.048, t GGE = -1.234 to 2.017, all p FDR >.05) in either patient group. Significance Overall, although sex differences in behavioral and clinical outcomes of epilepsy have been consistently reported in previous studies, our results indicate that sex-related clinical differences in epilepsy are not strongly captured by macroscale structural magnetic resonance imaging measures, and may instead arise from hormonal, neurochemical, or functional-network mechanisms.

title: Non-contrast MRI reliably captures perfusion abnormalities in status epilepticus.
abstract: Objective To determine whether non-contrast pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) detects status epilepticus (SE)-related perfusion abnormalities and shows quantitative correspondence with dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to compare single-slice and volumetric approaches for asymmetry assessment. Methods Adult patients from a prospectively recruited single-center SE cohort were included in this retrospective analysis when MRI was performed within 48 h after clinical SE onset and both pCASL and DSC perfusion sequences were available. Visual assessment was pCASL-led, with corresponding DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF) and cerebral blood volume (CBV) maps subsequently evaluated. Perfusion asymmetry was quantified using mirrored contralateral reference regions. Single-slice peak-abnormality and volumetric segmentation approaches were applied to pCASL, DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF), and cerebral blood volume (CBV). Results Of 982 individuals with SE, 180 underwent MRI including pCASL and DSC within 48 h. pCASL-led assessment identified SE-related perfusion abnormalities in 75 of 180 (42%): hyperperfusion in 65, hypoperfusion in 6, and pCASL-DSC discordance in 4. Corresponding DSC abnormalities were present in 71 of 75 (95%). Thus, quantitative asymmetry analysis was performed in 71 unilateral evaluable cases. In the hyperperfusion subgroup, pCASL asymmetry correlated significantly with DSC-derived CBF using both volumetric and single-slice assessment (ρ = .558 and ρ = .571, respectively; both p < .001), and with DSC-derived CBV (ρ = .495 and ρ = .374, respectively; p < .001 and p = .003). Single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry showed strong correspondence (ρ = .773, p < .001). No significant difference was observed between single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry after correction for multiple comparisons. Significance Non-contrast pCASL detected SE-related peri-ictal perfusion abnormalities and showed significant quantitative correspondence with DSC-derived CBF and CBV in parenchymal hyperperfusion. Single-slice pCASL asymmetry showed strong agreement with volumetric assessment, supporting its use as a pragmatic approach for clinically oriented evaluation.

Adult patients from a prospectively recruited single-center SE cohort were included in this retrospective analysis when MRI was performed within 48 h after clinical SE onset and both pCASL and DSC perfusion sequences were available. Perfusion asymmetry was quantified using mirrored contralateral reference regions. Single-slice peak-abnormality and volumetric segmentation approaches were applied to pCASL, DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF), and cerebral blood volume (CBV).

Of 982 individuals with SE, 180 underwent MRI including pCASL and DSC within 48 h. pCASL-led assessment identified SE-related perfusion abnormalities in 75 of 180 (42%): hyperperfusion in 65, hypoperfusion in 6, and pCASL-DSC discordance in 4. title: Stereoelectroencephalography-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: Results from more than 20 years of experience.
abstract: Objective This study was undertaken to present more than 2 decades of experience with stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG)-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC) in focal drug-resistant epilepsy and to identify clinical, electrophysiological, and procedural predictors of treatment response. Methods We retrospectively studied 244 consecutive patients treated with SEEG-guided RF-TC at our center between 2001 and 2024. All had at least 2 months of follow-up, and 240 (98.4%) completed 1 year. Outcomes were assessed at 2, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was seizure freedom at 2 months and 1 year without additional surgery, and the secondary endpoint was ≥50% seizure reduction. Demographic and epilepsy-, imaging-, and procedure-related variables were analyzed. Results At 2 months, 160 patients (65.6%) were responders, including 63 (25.8%) seizure-free. At 1 year, among 135 patients treated exclusively with SEEG-guided RF-TC, 64 (51.2%) were responders, including 19 (14.1%) seizure-free. At 5 years, 6.1% treated exclusively with SEEG-guided RF-TC remained seizure-free. Magnetic resonance imaging was negative in 40.6%, and focal cortical dysplasia was the most frequent imaging finding (20.1%). A higher number of contacts was associated with lower seizure-free rates at 1 year (p = .046). Pathology and electrode number were the only variables associated with 1-year outcomes. The positive predictive value of being a responder at 2 months for favorable surgical outcome was 83%, and the negative predictive value was 44%. Recoagulation within the first year was strongly associated with clinical improvement (p < .00001). Neurological complications occurred in 2.9%, including .8% permanent deficits. Significance SEEG-guided RF-TC is a safe diagnostic option with some therapeutic implication (6% seizure freedom in 5 years) for selected patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Early response predicts favorable long-term outcomes, and repeated coagulation can enhance clinical results. Pathology and the number of contacts used in thermocoagulation may serve as potential prognostic factors.
